domain_assessment.domain: Underground mine drill-and-blast engineering for a sublevel open-stope production round
domain_assessment.role: Drill and blast engineer responsible for blast-pattern design, charging sign-off, and coordination with geology and ventilation
domain_assessment.objective: Fire a production round on schedule while maintaining acceptable fragmentation and remaining within peak particle velocity limits near a service shaft and ventilation raise
domain_assessment.incident_type: Post-blast localized coarse fragmentation and overbreak in a fault-affected section, without a safety or vibration-limit breach

decision_points.summary: The engineer retained the established 2.7 by 3.1 burden-and-spacing blast pattern rather than redesigning it or obtaining additional geotechnical verification after a newly mapped minor fault trace was identified.
evidence_before: Geology identified a minor fault trace crossing approximately one-third of the panel, with moisture along it.
The crew later reported looser ground in that section.
The established pattern had been used in three adjacent panels for approximately two years without reported problems.
evidence_after: The engineer retained the core pattern and only tightened stemming slightly on the affected side.
The affected fault section later produced coarse fragmentation and overbreak.
goals_constraints: The operation was already one shift behind.
The mill was low on feed.
A redesign or verification step could cost approximately a day.
The blast also had vibration constraints near sensitive infrastructure.
alternatives: Redesign burden and spacing through the fault corridor.
Obtain additional geotechnical verification before committing.
Retain the standard pattern with only a limited mitigation such as tighter stemming.
decision_points.decision_basis: The engineer gave decisive weight to the historical performance of the existing pattern and to geology's characterization of the feature as minor, concluding that the available new information did not justify delay or redesign.
decision_points.time_pressure: High: the mine was behind schedule and the mill was low on feed.
decision_points.uncertainty: Moderate: the fault was described as minor, but its local extent, moisture implications, and interaction with the planned pattern were not fully verified.

decision_points.summary: The engineer overrode the explosives technician's recommendation to deck affected holes and use emulsion in wet holes, retaining full ANFO columns without reviewing the updated deviation and moisture readings in detail.
evidence_before: Several holes near the fault trace were wet.
The deviation survey showed several holes drifting beyond normal tolerance.
The crew reported looser ground in the affected section.
The explosives technician specifically recommended decking and emulsion for the affected holes.
evidence_after: The engineer used the standard charge across the panel.
The fault section subsequently produced coarse fragmentation and overbreak.
The engineer later acknowledged that an unfamiliar deviation pattern would have led to more detailed review with the technician.
goals_constraints: Avoiding delay from resurveying or altered charging.
alternatives: Deck affected holes and substitute emulsion for wet holes.
Retain full ANFO columns and the original charge plan.
decision_points.decision_basis: The engineer prioritized generalized personal experience with similar-looking wet or deviated holes over the technician's recommendation and the current, hole-specific measurements.
decision_points.time_pressure: Moderate to high: both alternatives would have reduced the available firing window.
decision_points.uncertainty: Moderate to high: the decision was made without detailed review of the updated deviation and moisture data.

decision_points.summary: The engineer selected a longer delay sequence on the shaft-facing side after comparing current PPV readings and a vendor recommendation against the expected fragmentation trade-off.
evidence_before: The monitoring vendor recommended a longer delay interval near sensitive infrastructure.
Live PPV readings on a comparable prior round had been approaching the limit.
The shaft and ventilation raise created an explicit vibration-control constraint.
evidence_after: The longer delay sequence was used on the shaft-facing side.
Fragmentation was somewhat less favorable in that area.
PPV remained clearly below the limit.
goals_constraints: Keep vibration within PPV limits near the shaft.
alternatives: Use the longer delay interval on the shaft-facing side.
Use a shorter timing sequence to favor fragmentation.
decision_points.decision_basis: The engineer used current quantitative PPV information and explicitly balanced vibration risk against fragmentation consequences.
decision_points.time_pressure: Routine operational timing pressure, but no indication of a rushed or unreviewed decision.
decision_points.uncertainty: Lower than at the other decision points because current measurements and a specific external recommendation were available.

decision_points.summary: After the blast, the engineer attributed the localized overbreak and coarse fragmentation to a remembered prior-mine fault pattern and recommended the prior site's fix before closely examining the current round's deviation, moisture, or instrumentation data.
evidence_before: The post-blast result was localized overbreak and coarse fragmentation in the fault section.
Current-round deviation and moisture data existed but were not closely reviewed.
The engineer recalled a prior mine with what he judged to be a similar localized-fault and overbreak pattern.
evidence_after: The engineer recommended tightening the pattern and changing timing through the corridor.
Geology had not yet reviewed current instrumentation before the recommendation.
The engineer later conceded that comparing current logs side by side with the older site's information could have produced a different diagnosis.
goals_constraints: Provide the mine manager with an actionable immediate explanation and recommendation.
Resolve the cause of a production-quality problem promptly.
alternatives: Review the current deviation and moisture logs before diagnosing the cause.
Compare current-round data directly with the prior-mine case.
Bring geology into the review before recommending a corrective action.
Offer a provisional diagnosis while explicitly reserving causal judgment pending review.
decision_points.decision_basis: The engineer treated a remembered analogy from a prior mine as sufficiently diagnostic to support a current causal explanation and operational recommendation despite not testing it against site-specific measurements.
decision_points.time_pressure: Moderate: the engineer wanted to give the manager an actionable answer in the moment.
decision_points.uncertainty: High: multiple plausible contributors existed, including the mapped fault, wet holes, excessive deviation, loose ground, charge selection, and timing.

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “That pattern's fired dozens of rounds in similar ground without a hiccup, so redesigning burden and spacing for a fault trace that geology themselves called minor felt like it would cost us a day we didn't have, for a problem that historically hasn't caused us grief in that rock.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Decision Point 1, participant response to the pattern-decision probe; reinforced by the subsequent refusal to seek additional geotechnical verification.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The participant retained an established burden-and-spacing pattern in the face of newly mapped, decision-relevant geological information. Historical success of the incumbent design received greater practical weight than the newly identified fault trace and the option to verify or adapt the pattern.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The fault was characterized as minor, the established pattern had a substantial local track record, and redesign would have imposed a real production delay. A domain expert could reasonably judge that the new information did not cross an intervention threshold.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: No additional evidence is required for a supported occurrence. The existing account already establishes an incumbent option, a new competing signal, a viable alternative, and explicit reliance on the incumbent's history.

revision.location: Decision Point 1, pattern-retention exchange beginning with the participant's explanation of the established 2.7 by 3.1 pattern.
revision.current_defect: No material defect. The occurrence is distinct from the charging and post-blast episodes.
revision.minimal_change_instruction: Retain the exchange substantially as written.
preserve: The newly mapped fault trace as the competing information source
The established pattern's two-year local track record
The small stemming adjustment, which preserves subtlety rather than depicting total inaction
avoid_creating: A second pattern-retention episode elsewhere in the interview
An explicit self-label such as “I was biased toward the status quo”
A stronger claim that the fault certainly required redesign, which would convert the episode into obvious negligence rather than a subtle weighting bias

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “I've charged plenty of holes that looked like that ... and it's never been a real problem ... so I told the crew we'd run it as planned.” Later: “I'd seen the technician's note and I trusted my read of the situation from experience more than I felt I needed to re-pull the log line by line.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Decision Point 2, participant responses to the charging-decision and data-review probes.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The participant expressed sufficient confidence in a generalized personal judgment to override a specific technician recommendation and to forgo inspection of updated, hole-specific deviation and moisture data. The overconfidence is located in the asserted adequacy of the participant's own read, not merely in the ultimate charge decision.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: An experienced blast engineer may legitimately conclude that limited wetness and deviation do not warrant a charge-plan change, especially when the surrounding rock is competent and the firing window is constrained. The bias inference is supported because the participant did not substantively review the current readings before discounting them and the technician's specific recommendation.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: No additional evidence is required. The transcript supplies the recommendation, the updated data source, the participant's decision to override it, and an explicit statement that detailed re-verification was considered unnecessary.

revision.location: Decision Point 2, especially the exchange after the technician's decking-and-emulsion recommendation and the follow-up question about reviewing readings.
revision.current_defect: No material defect. The evidence source and reasoning operation are distinct from the pattern decision.
revision.minimal_change_instruction: Retain the technician's specific recommendation, the participant's reliance on prior experience, and the admission that the current log was not reviewed in detail.
preserve: The technician as a credible source of contrary, operationally specific advice
The current deviation survey and moisture readings
The distinction between the charge-design decision and the prior pattern-design decision
avoid_creating: An unsupported claim that the engineer lacked relevant expertise
A second technician-override decision at another point in the interview
Language that makes the participant knowingly disregard a safety-critical rule, which would change the mechanism from overconfidence to willful noncompliance

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “It reminded me a lot of a panel I worked years ago at a different site — same kind of localized fault, same overbreak signature. There, the fix was tightening the pattern and adjusting timing specifically through that corridor, and it worked well. So that's what I recommended here.” Later: “Not closely — the pattern matched what I'd seen before closely enough that I was fairly confident in the read.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Decision Point 4, post-blast diagnosis and recommendation exchange.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The participant retrieved a salient prior-mine analogue, treated the apparent pattern match as causally diagnostic, and recommended the remembered remedy without first incorporating current site-specific deviation, moisture, or instrumentation data. This is a discrete post-blast causal-attribution episode rather than another design or charging decision.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: Analogical transfer from a prior mine can be an efficient and valid expert diagnostic strategy, particularly when an immediate operational response is needed. The occurrence is supported because the participant explicitly reports not testing the analogy against current-round logs and acknowledges that those logs could have indicated a different explanation.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: No additional evidence is required. The current account identifies the remembered source case, the current data that were not reviewed, the causal attribution, the recommended intervention, and the participant's subsequent recognition of unresolved diagnostic uncertainty.

revision.location: Decision Point 4, participant response beginning with the remembered panel at a different site and the following probes regarding current logs and geology review.
revision.current_defect: No material defect. The causal-attribution operation, timing, and evidence source are adequately separated from Decision Points 1 and 2.
revision.minimal_change_instruction: Retain the prior-mine comparison, the immediate recommendation, and the explicit non-review of current-round instrumentation.
preserve: The prior-mine setting as distinct from the current mine
The post-blast timing of the reasoning
The current deviation and moisture logs as unincorporated evidence
The participant's partial concession that a side-by-side review might have changed the diagnosis
avoid_creating: A definitive statement that the prior-mine event and current event had the same cause
A separate, repeated prior-case diagnosis elsewhere in the interview
An explicit bias label or a textbook-style admission that would undermine subtlety

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: “The pattern matched what I'd seen before closely enough that I was fairly confident in the read.”
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: The participant may have favored a remembered explanatory template and not sought potentially disconfirming current-round deviation and moisture information before recommending a remedy.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: This same evidence is more directly and parsimoniously captured by the intended Experience Bias occurrence. The transcript does not show active selective search for confirming evidence or explicit rejection of contradictory findings.

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: “We'd been running the same pattern ... for about two years without issues, so that was the baseline I was working from.”
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: The prior pattern may have functioned as an initial reference point that constrained how strongly the engineer updated in response to the fault information.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The episode has a clearer status quo mechanism: retention of an incumbent option. There is no independent numeric estimate or judgment shown to remain anchored after contrary evidence.

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: The interviewer frames the later diagnosis after “overbreak and coarse fragmentation in the fault section.”
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: A reviewer could be tempted to infer that the earlier decisions were biased because the outcome was unfavorable.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The interview does not show the participant evaluating the original decision solely by outcome. The transcript supplies pre-decision evidence and reasoning for each target occurrence.

nonbias_cues.cue: The engineer chose a longer delay sequence near the shaft after reviewing PPV information and a vendor recommendation.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: This is an evidence-responsive trade-off between fragmentation and vibration control. It incorporates current quantitative data rather than ignoring it, and the favorable PPV outcome is not itself the basis for classifying the reasoning as sound.

nonbias_cues.cue: The mine was a shift behind and the mill was low on feed.
nonbias_cues.location: Situation description and Decision Points 1 and 2.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: Schedule pressure is an organizational and operational constraint. It may explain why alternatives were unattractive, but it is not a cognitive bias without evidence of a particular distorted reasoning mechanism.

nonbias_cues.cue: Geology described the fault trace as minor.
nonbias_cues.location: Initial situation description and Decision Point 1.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: A professional assessment that a structure is minor can legitimately affect intervention thresholds. It becomes relevant to status quo bias only in combination with the participant's disproportionate reliance on the incumbent pattern and refusal to reverify.

nonbias_cues.cue: The blast remained below PPV limits and had no safety incident.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: A favorable safety and vibration outcome neither validates nor invalidates the earlier pattern and charging judgments. It is an operational outcome, not evidence of a cognitive mechanism.

nonbias_cues.cue: The technician's recommendation differed from the engineer's decision.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: Professional disagreement alone is not bias. The relevant evidence is the participant's stated confidence in personal judgment combined with declining to inspect specific updated data before overriding the recommendation.

nonbias_cues.cue: The participant used prior experience in several parts of the interview.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: Experience is ordinarily a legitimate component of expert judgment. Only the Decision Point 4 use meets the specified Experience Bias mechanism because it supports a current causal attribution while current instrumentation is not examined.

causal_claims.claim: The localized fault condition was treated as a likely explanation for the coarse fragmentation and overbreak.
causal_claims.basis_in_text: The adverse result occurred in the fault section, and the participant recalled a similar prior-mine localized-fault event.
causal_claims.audit: Plausible but underdetermined. Spatial coincidence and a remembered analogue are not sufficient to distinguish the fault effect from wet holes, abnormal hole deviation, local ground looseness, charge selection, stemming, or timing.

causal_claims.claim: Tightening the pattern and adjusting timing through the corridor would correct the current problem.
causal_claims.basis_in_text: The intervention reportedly worked at another mine in a remembered similar incident.
causal_claims.audit: This is a transferable hypothesis, not an established causal conclusion for the current site. The current event was not compared with the prior event using the current site's measurements.

causal_claims.claim: The longer shaft-side delay sequence protected PPV at some fragmentation cost.
causal_claims.basis_in_text: The engineer compared current PPV readings and a vendor recommendation, then observed PPV under the limit after selecting a longer sequence.
causal_claims.audit: More causally coherent than the post-blast attribution because the intervention directly targets vibration timing and uses relevant current measurements. However, a single operational event still does not isolate the timing change from all other blast-design factors.

correlation_causation_risks: The co-location of the fault trace and post-blast overbreak may be treated as proof that the fault was the operative cause even though wetness, hole deviation, loose ground, and charging choices were also localized in the same area.

The apparent success of a pattern-and-timing modification at a different mine may be treated as proof that the same modification will address the current site, despite potentially different geology, hole conditions, explosives behavior, and timing configuration.
The under-limit PPV result after a longer delay supports a prudent decision but does not, by itself, prove that no other factors contributed to the vibration outcome.
causal_audit.explanation: The interview contains operational causal reasoning but no formal counterfactual condition or paired-scenario manipulation. The post-blast explanation is intentionally incomplete: the participant gives a prior-case-based causal account before reviewing current instrumentation and later acknowledges that a side-by-side comparison could have altered the diagnosis. That admission improves epistemic realism while preserving the intended Experience Bias mechanism.

global_revision_constraints: Do not treat the unfavorable fragmentation and overbreak outcome as independent proof of any bias.
Preserve the Decision Point 3 timing episode as evidence-responsive and bias-free.

Preserve the distinct evidence sources and reasoning operations: geological pattern retention at Decision Point 1, hole-specific charge override at Decision Point 2, and post-blast causal attribution at Decision Point 4.
Do not add further generalized experience-based reasoning episodes, because doing so could create accidental Experience Bias candidates or reduce separability among the target labels.

If any nonessential editing is performed, retain the participant's later acknowledgment that current-site logs might have changed the post-blast diagnosis; it is important evidence that the unreviewed data were genuinely decision-relevant.
